questions.q: What is a variable best described as?
options: A labeled box in memory that stores a value
A program that runs by itself
questions.explain: A variable is a labeled box: the label is its name, and what's inside is its value.

questions.q: In this code, what is the name of the variable?
questions.explain: The name is the label on the box. Here the label is score.

questions.q: In score = 10, what does the = sign do?
options: Checks if two things are equal
Puts the value into the box
questions.explain: In code, = means "put this into the box", not "equals" like in math.

questions.q: How do you create a variable in Python?
options: Write the name, then =, then the value
questions.explain: Python needs no special keyword. Writing name = value creates the box and fills it.

questions.q: Which of these is a valid variable name?
questions.explain: No spaces, dashes or symbols are allowed. player_name uses only letters and an underscore.

questions.q: Why is it called a "variable"?
options: Because its name can be very long
questions.explain: You can swap the contents of the box, so the value can vary.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT allowed in a variable name?
questions.explain: Python thinks a space means a new word has started, so spaces are not allowed.

questions.q: Which name follows Python's snake_case style?
questions.explain: snake_case uses lowercase words joined by underscores: total_price.

questions.q: In this code, what is the value stored in the box?
questions.explain: The value is what's inside the box. The name is player_name, the value is "Sam".

questions.q: Which name is NOT allowed because it starts with a number?
questions.explain: Numbers are fine inside a name (player1), but a name can't start with one.

questions.q: What is the relationship between score and Score?
options: One of them causes an error
questions.explain: Capital letters matter. score and Score are two completely different boxes.

questions.q: Why is total-price not a valid variable name?
questions.explain: Python reads total-price as total minus price.

questions.q: Which is the best name for a variable that stores a user's age?
questions.explain: Good names describe what's inside the box. user_age says exactly what it holds.

questions.q: After running this code, what does score hold?
questions.explain: The second line swaps the contents of the box. The old value 10 is replaced by 11.

questions.q: Which name is allowed?
questions.explain: Underscores are allowed. The others have a space, start with a number, or are a keyword.

questions.q: Why can't you name a variable class?
options: It already has a special job in Python (it's a keyword)
questions.explain: Keywords already have a special meaning, like naming your shop "STOP".

questions.q: Which is the snake_case version of "first name"?
questions.explain: Lowercase words joined by an underscore: first_name.

questions.q: Which is a real benefit of variables?
options: You can change a value in one place instead of many
They remove the need for names
questions.explain: If the tax rate changes, you update the one box instead of hunting through hundreds of lines.

questions.q: Which name is valid?
questions.explain: score2 only uses letters and a number, and the number isn't first.

questions.q: Which name is legal but unhelpful?
questions.explain: x is allowed, but it doesn't tell you what it holds. The other two are not allowed at all.

questions.q: What does lives hold after this code runs?
questions.explain: Python takes the 3 out of the box, subtracts 1 to get 2, and puts 2 back in.

questions.q: Which line would cause an error?
questions.explain: Only letters, numbers and underscores are allowed, so the $ breaks the rules. (Some other languages allow $, but Python doesn't.)

questions.q: The code below tries to use a variable called Score. What happens?
options: It errors, because there is no box named Score
questions.explain: Capital letters matter. Only score exists, so asking for Score finds no box (Python shows a NameError).

questions.q:
How many of these names are NOT valid?

first name   3rd_place   class   first_name_
questions.explain: first name has a space, 3rd_place starts with a number, and class is a keyword. first_name_ is fine.

questions.q: Which is the best name for a variable that stores the number of items in a shopping cart?
questions.explain: cart_item_count is valid, descriptive, and uses snake_case. cart-items isn't allowed because of the dash.

questions.q: Which pair of names refers to TWO different variables?
questions.explain: Capital letters matter, so Total and total are different boxes.

questions.q: What does final_price hold?
questions.explain: Python reads the values inside the price and discount boxes: 20 - 5 = 15.

questions.q: Which statement is TRUE?
options: Capital letters are ignored in names
questions.explain: Underscores are allowed. Capitals matter, numbers are fine if not first, and = means "put into the box".

questions.q: What does x hold after this code runs?
questions.explain: Step by step: x starts at 4, then becomes 5, then 5 * 2 = 10.

questions.q: This line fails. Why, and what's the best fix?
options: It needs a number, so change "Math" to 5
class is a reserved keyword, so rename it (for example subject)
The = sign is wrong, so use ==
Variable names must be uppercase, so use CLASS
questions.explain: class already has a special job in Python, so you need a different name such as subject.
